Stage 1 admits these two Kanagawa performances because Eitetsu Hayashi's 55th-performance-year program combines a major living taiko innovator with his Fu-un no Kai lineage, special guest Hiromitsu Agatsuma on Tsugaru shamisen, and a newly commissioned work listed by the presenting foundation. That concrete lineage, instrumental identity, anniversary context, and commission clear RADAR admission independently of fame. Stage 2 assigns A+ to both: actively make room if Greater Tokyo/Kanto is in play. Scarcity was challenged explicitly: the same core program has two confirmed Kanagawa performances, and neither is billed as a farewell, final appearance, or one-time-only last chance. The 55th anniversary and lineup are unusually compelling, but A+ still captures the recommendation without stretching S. Recent/current intake remains centered on A and A+ with scarcity tiers reserved for demonstrably harder-to-repeat moments; this batch adds A 0 / A+ 2 / S 0 / S+ 0 without treating distribution as a quota.

events.factual_description: Kanagawa Kenmin Hall's official presentation page lists Eitetsu Hayashi's 55th-performance-year concert in Yokosuka on Friday, October 9, 2026, at Yokosuka Arts Theatre, with doors at 18:00 and the performance at 18:30. The billed performers are Hayashi on taiko; EITETSU FU-UN no KAI members Hideichiro Ueda, Mikita Hase, Makoto Tashiro and Yu Tsuji on taiko; and special guest Hiromitsu Agatsuma on Tsugaru shamisen. The listed program includes Agatsuma's NIPPON and YOSARE plus a new work commissioned by Kanagawa Kenmin Hall. Reserved tickets are listed at ¥4,500 for S seats and ¥3,500 for A seats.

en.why_it_matters: This is a lineage-and-sound event, not a generic anniversary. Hayashi marks 55 years of performance alongside Fu-un no Kai, the taiko ensemble formed around his work, while Agatsuma brings the cutting attack and pitch-bending language of Tsugaru shamisen into the same frame. A new Kanagawa-commissioned work keeps the program pointed toward transmission and expansion rather than nostalgia alone.
en.trip_verdict: If Greater Tokyo/Kanto is in play on October 9, actively make room for Yokosuka and let the theatre anchor the evening. Because the same core program has a second confirmed Kanagawa performance in Odawara on November 14, choose the date that fits the trip rather than bending the entire itinerary around one of the two.
